A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NC-GCD, with matching methods and experiments despite title and layout changes. All pages support comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 includes Appendices A–F.

before.justification: V1 reports original NC-GCD benchmark results, component ablations, an alpha-sensitivity experiment, and feature visualizations in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds backbone comparisons, sensitivity experiments, category-count estimates, and computational measurements in its appendices.

M1.justification: The fixed ETF prototypes, supervised and unsupervised alignment losses, representation-learning objective, and SCM procedure are retained. V2's SCM pseudocode and category-count estimation recipe further specify existing operations; the PDFs do not establish an underlying method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GCD on CUB-200, Stanford Cars, FGVC Aircraft, Herbarium19, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100. V2's additional experiments vary backbones and clustering parameters within this retained coverage; its suggested application domains are not evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds TRAILER to the known-K fine-grained comparisons in Table 1 and reports ProtoGCD and RLCD in the CUB backbone comparison in Table 8. These extend the existing comparator set. SelEx already appears in v1 Table 1 and is not a new baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds experiments using DINOv2 and CLIP, beta values of 0.5, 1, and 2 with best-versus-final accuracy reporting, K perturbations of ±10% and ±20%, and clustering periods of 1, 5, 10, and 20 epochs. These introduce substantial evaluation settings; newly disclosed defaults for retained experiments are separate reproducibility additions.

E4.justification: Appendices B–D add evidence about loss-weight sensitivity, incorrect category counts, clustering frequency, computational efficiency, and feature evolution. The training visualization is extended with additional epochs and a three-category trajectory. The ETF-alignment configuration scores in Tables 6–7 already appeared in v1 Table 3 and are not new ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions mention a fixed seed for category splits, but neither reports repeated-training run counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds backbone, sensitivity, category-count, parameter-count, and timing results, including CUB All accuracy of 87.9% with DINOv2 and 78.5% with CLIP. Main Table 1 NC-GCD scores remain unchanged. Section 5.2 corrects v1's CIFAR-100/ImageNet-100 accuracy statements from 88.7%/94.1% to 82.7%/88.4%, matching the existing tables, and several improvement rows are corrected.

T1.justification: The principal ETF definitions, neural-collapse statements, and method equations are retained. Section 4.2 newly specifies q_i as zero-sum, mutually orthonormal unit vectors in a K−1-dimensional space. These added conditions are mathematically incompatible, constituting a problematic formal addition. No new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that fixed ETF prototypes unify supervised and unsupervised optimization, SCM stabilizes assignments, and NC-GCD improves category separation and novel-category accuracy across six benchmarks. Exchanges between 'strong' and 'state-of-the-art' wording do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking K underestimation to insufficient prototype capacity, beta and clustering frequency to stability–adaptation tradeoffs, and CLIP gains to complementary semantic and geometric alignment. Appendix E newly acknowledges unvalidated scalability and sensitivity of category-count estimation to feature quality. These substantially expand mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 supplies optimizer momentum, cosine scheduling, a 200-epoch budget, clustering period, weighted sampling, category split counts, SCM pseudocode, and the 30-epoch category-count estimation procedure. It also reports parameter counts and execution times. The stated GPU changes from A6000 to RTX 3090; this reporting revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The existing related-work argument is extended with RLCD, ProtoGCD, continual GCD, and domain-incremental research. V2 explicitly contrasts NC-GCD with TRAILER's fixed classifier and cross-entropy alignment. It also adds a SelEx reference and replaces several background citations, without fundamentally reorganizing the research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, updates affiliations and correspondence information, standardizes much of the class/category terminology, and edits several passages and cross-references. It adds acknowledgements and appendix navigation and moves training-visualization discussion into the appendix. Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout, merges v1 Figures 1–2 into a composite overview, and redraws the framework diagram. It condenses the main ETF ablation table while redisplaying the full results in appendix tables, expands the training figure, and adds several tables and plots. The alpha plot is unchanged apart from placement and numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves reproducibility and scrutiny of the fixed-prototype approach by supplying previously absent training and K-estimation details, testing sensitivity to key assumptions, evaluating additional backbones, and stating limitations. It also corrects misleading main-text accuracy statements. These gains outweigh new reporting problems, including Table 11's PIM Stanford Cars score conflicting with Table 1 and the incompatible q_i conditions in Section 4.2, which still require correction.
